note: Coordinates whose VALUE Conduit constructs, even though an Apollo Hub established the coordinate. These serve with @provenance(tier: OBSERVED, valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE) per ADR 0007. Before that record there was no way to say this, so these values shipped under a bare OBSERVED annotation that told clients an Apollo Hub had answered with them. It had not. This file is the correction.
whyThisIsNotTheSameAsAnInvention: The identifier GRAMMAR is published. The pinned OpenAPI snapshot carries ri.apollo.main.environment.123, ri.apollo.main.installation.123 and ri.apollo.main.package.123, plus ri.autopilot.main.team.123 showing the service segment varies by owning service. Conduit follows that grammar rather than inventing one. What Conduit supplies is the locator, and for entity ids the meaning of one segment. Those parts are registered in docs/evidence/conduit-inventions.json.
citationForm: Each entry names the Go function that mints the value and the published example the grammar is taken from. A coordinate here must already exist in the recovery record: this file changes how a recovered coordinate's value is described, and can never add a coordinate.

ApolloEnvironment.rid.conduitSupplies: the locator, as the first 12 bytes of a SHA-256 over the environment id, hex encoded. Apollo's example locator is the placeholder 123 and the one documented Apollo locator elsewhere is a UUID, so no format is established and this one is Conduit's choice.

ApolloEntity.packageRid.mintedBy: internal/apollo/application/service.go, packageRID at the installation projection
ApolloEntity.packageRid.conduitSupplies: the locator, as above, over the product coordinate.

ApolloEntity.id.grammarPublishedAs: apollo-openapi aeid:apollo-environment-demo:helm-chart:wordpress, in the ListInstallations and GetInstallation response examples
ApolloEntity.id.conduitSupplies: the value only. The shape is Apollo's published one -- same segment count, same helm-chart product type, and an environment in the second segment -- but the string is composed from Conduit's own environment and entity names rather than answered by a Hub.

ApolloProductDependency.optional.grammarPublishedAs: apollo-openapi ProductDependency.optional, typed boolean and NOT in the schema's required set; the recovered GraphQL coordinate is a String, so no scalar type is established for the GraphQL side either
ApolloProductDependency.optional.conduitSupplies: both the default and the rendering. Neither pinned publish request -- PublishHelmChartRequest nor PublishServiceRequest -- carries an optionality input, so a publicly published dependency has no publisher declaration and Conduit answers Conduit's own default, false. catalog.Dependency.Optional is a plain bool, so a declared false and an undeclared one are the same stored value and cannot be told apart on read. The strings "true" and "false" are Conduit's rendering of that bool into the String the recovered coordinate declares.

ApolloProduct.rid.grammarPublishedAs: apollo-openapi ri.autopilot.main.team.123, which shows the service segment naming the service that owns the resource. Apollo publishes no type token for a Product, so the namespace is Conduit's own rather than a guess inside ri.apollo.
ApolloProduct.rid.conduitSupplies: the whole identifier. The service segment is conduit because a Product that exists only in Conduit is owned by Conduit; the type token and the locator are Conduit's.

ApolloProductRelease.rid.conduitSupplies: the whole identifier, keyed on the Maven coordinate Apollo already treats as the release's identity.

whyAnEntryNeedNotNameAnInvention: Two different claims are being kept apart here. 'Conduit built this value' is what valueTier discloses, and it is true of every coordinate in this file. 'Conduit invented this shape' is a stronger claim, true of some of them, and it belongs in the invention register. ApolloEntity.id used to name an invention that turned out to be a misreading -- the shape was Apollo's all along -- and requiring an invention on every entry would have forced a replacement guess rather than allowing the honest answer, which is that there is nothing invented left to register.
